required_facts.fact: Immediately after the events at Sanctuary on Horizon, evidence recovered from Kai Leng's trail - or a tracer planted by Miranda Lawson if she survived - lets the Alliance locate the Illusive Man's headquarters: Cronos Station, a Cerberus space station orbiting the variable star Anadius in the Horsehead Nebula. Admiral Hackett masses a fleet while Commander Shepard leads a boarding assault with EDI as a required squadmate. The team fights through hangar bays and burning corridors against Assault Troopers, Centurions, Guardians, Phantoms, Nemeses and Atlas mechs; if Legion was sold to Cerberus it appears as a hostile Legion assassin, and a captured Jack can be freed along the way. Cerberus data terminals and the salvaged remains of the Human-Reaper larva from the Collector Base reveal that the Illusive Man had been hoarding and studying Reaper and Collector technology, was himself indoctrinated, and had experimented on his own personnel; other records expose the origin of EDI, assembled from the rogue Alliance VI and technology salvaged from Sovereign. In the station's inner chamber Kai Leng ambushes Shepard for a final duel. Shepard defeats him, and when the wounded assassin attempts a stealth kill from behind, Shepard counters and kills him with an omni-blade, able to dedicate the kill to Thane Krios, Miranda Lawson or Major Kirrahe depending on who died at his hands. Shepard recovers the Prothean VI Vendetta and the complete Catalyst plans, but the Illusive Man has already fled to the Citadel. Admiral Anderson confirms that the Citadel has been moved into orbit of Earth, and Priority: Earth becomes the only remaining mission, beginning the endgame.

The Horse Head Nebula was a star cluster of mostly uninhabited, barely-surveyed planets with modest resourcing prospects. Though within Earth Systems Alliance space and near Citadel space, it sat in a legal grey area for Citadel races; Noveria, one of its worlds, was not part of Citadel space. Cerberus maintained major operations in the cluster: Minuteman Station was located there in 2185, and by 2186 the organization's headquarters (Cronos Station) and at least one outpost lay in out-of-the-way positions within the nebula. Its systems included Pax (containing Noveria), Anadius (containing Cronos Station), Fortuna, Strenuus and Maganlis. Missions set here included the Noveria arc in Mass Effect and Priority: Cerberus Headquarters and N7: Cerberus Fighter Base in Mass Effect 3. The real-world nebula is Barnard 33 in IC 434, first identified by Williamina Fleming in 1888; Mass Effect 3 renders the name "Horsehead Nebula" without the space. After acquiring the Normandy SR-2, the Minuteman Station and its surrounding cluster became inaccessible.

Space stations are artificial structures built and maintained to support space travel, defence, or resource gathering. Humans built a large number of them as military installations during their expansion through the Milky Way, valuing their proximity to mass relays. Stations may be constructed from scratch or built onto existing bodies such as asteroids, and normally hold a fixed position within a system or orbit a planet. Large structures like the Citadel, which does not orbit a fixed point, use navigation systems and engines to maintain position. Most stations include drive discharge points so visiting ships can safely dump their core charge. Because of their expense, stations are frequently repurposed.

The page groups stations into broad categories. Trade/Gateway stations sit near relay nexuses and become commerce and communications hubs with docking facilities; some, such as those around Pluto, develop sizable populations, and orbital ports like the planned Asteroid X57 provide transfer points for goods and travellers. Defence stations in orbit around colonies give early warning of attack and allow control of the ground situation; Noveria's orbital battle stations can target and destroy approaching vessels and strike surface targets with antimatter warheads. Research stations offer platforms for long-term or low-gravity experiments, astronomical observation, and work too dangerous or classified for a colony, such as AI development or BAaT's biotic training, with the option of destroying the station to contain a catastrophic breach.

The article lists many known Milky Way stations, including Arcturus Station, Avernus Station, the Barn, the Citadel, Cronos Station, Gagarin Station (also called "Jump Zero"), the Jon Grissom Academy, the Lazarus Research Station, Minuteman Station, Omega, Pinnacle Station, and others, plus Khi Tasira and the Nexus in Andromeda.

Short page (under ~150 words of prose). Jana was the Illusive Man's assistant in 2186, drawn from the first edition of Mass Effect: Deception, a novel BioWare acknowledged contained lore discrepancies. Her duties included assigning Cerberus operatives to minor tasks, filtering the Illusive Man's calls and messages, and guiding the rare visitors permitted to meet him. She was described as having black hair, large brown eyes, and a full figure, and had been a military officer of unspecified affiliation before joining Cerberus. Kai Leng questioned how human Jana really was and believed the Illusive Man was grooming her for a greater role. A separate blonde-haired scientist also named Jana appears in Cronos Station video logs discussing indoctrination.

Short page: the Assault Captain was a Cerberus officer who led a squad of Assault Troopers into battle. Randall Ezno encountered him once, on the Barn space station, during his escape (in Mass Effect: Infiltrator). The Captain had considerable health and a strong regenerating shield, tended to stay in cover unless Shepard was in his line of sight, was vulnerable to headshots, and wore a jetpack that let him close to Eviscerator shotgun range; Pull could flush him from cover or interrupt him in flight. He resembled the Trooper and Assault Trooper in appearance.

evidence.text: After cementing the alliance between Cerberus and Aria, the Illusive Man dispatched research teams to construct bases on the other side of the Omega 4 Relay to scavenge for Reaper technology. Unfortunately, a new type of husks called Adjutants being held in captivity in those bases broke free and commandeered Cerberus vessels to begin an invasion of Omega. The Illusive Man dispatched General Oleg Petrovsky and Colonel Raymond Ashe to help Aria quell the assault. Though Aria and Petrovsky amassed a fleet to defend Omega from more Adjutants, Ashe, who was imprisoned for defying Aria's authority and fought his way free, called the Illusive Man to confirm that he's ready to start the real battle for Omega. After Aria and Petrovsky contain the Adjutant threat at Cerberus's Avernus Station beyond the Omega 4 Relay, the Illusive Man activates his true plan: the conquest of Omega. With Aria out of the way, the station's gangs are unable to mount a cohesive defense. Aria eventually does return by hijacking the Elbrus, Petrovsky's ship, and coordinates a guerrilla war against the Cerberus invaders. Petrovsky secures victory only when he threatens to order the Cerberus fleet to destroy the station. The Illusive Man's gambit succeeds. With Omega under his control, Cerberus now has exclusive access to the Omega 4 Relay and the center of the galaxy, a treasure trove of Reaper technology and potentially the safest location in the galaxy to weather the Reaper invasion. |  | ***“You've got to walk your own path...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Homeworlds** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text: The Illusive Man's plan to capture Omega was elegantly wrought. Experimental specimens called adjutants "escaped" from a Cerberus facility beyond the Omega\-4 mass relay, took command of a Cerberus convoy, and arrived on Omega to wreak havoc. With more adjutants incoming, Cerberus reached out to Aria T'Loak, claiming it needed her help to stop its wayward test subjects. Reluctantly offering her own forces in an alliance, Aria joined Cerberus's General Oleg Petrovsky aboard his ship to oversee the battle. When the adjutants overran the Cerberus\-Omega fleet, Petrovsky and Aria escaped through the Omega\-4 relay. However, Petrovsky's subordinate Colonel Raymond Ashe had remained behind on Omega to take control of the station's defenses while Cerberus reinforcements approached. Announcing that it was protecting the galaxy from the adjutant threat, Cerberus seized Omega, giving the Illusive Man full control of the Omega\-4 relay and the space beyond. Without Aria to keep them in line, the various criminal and mercenary factions on the station erupted, fighting both Cerberus ground troops and each other. Meanwhile, Aria was taken captive by General Petrovsky. Realizing that the adjutants had simply been a ruse to capture Omega, Aria managed to escape back to Omega, slipping away into its underbelly to organize a resistance force. Eventually, Petrovsky ordered the Cerberus forces to evacuate the station, but this was yet another ruse \-\- this time to lure Aria out of hiding. With his troops out of harm's way, Petrovsky summoned a massive Cerberus fleet and presented Aria with an ultimatum: leave Omega or lose it. Petrovsky threatened to destroy the station rather than lose control, and with no alternative, Aria left, vowing she would return to claim Omega and take her revenge.

evidence.text: Vendetta reveals that the Catalyst to be the Citadel but the Illusive Man had already fled there and thus alerted the Reapers of its intended purpose. Shepard finds the Illusive Man onboard the Citadel orbiting Earth, showing signs of Reaper modifications across his face. Using these upgrades to mimic indoctrination, the Illusive Man immobilizes and controls the motor functions of both Shepard and Anderson. He then forces Shepard to shoot Anderson in the gut to prove his powers. Despite Shepard asking him to let them stop the Reapers, the Illusive Man refuses to allow the Commander to undo his plans of controlling the Reapers. He claims that he is confident that he can control them, but when Shepard asks him if he is willing to bet humanity's existence on it his resistance begins to falter. He desperately argues that sacrifices had to be made, but Shepard counters by saying that he had sacrificed too much. However, when Shepard convinces the Illusive Man that he is under the Reapers' control and tells him to resist them, the Illusive Man replies that he "tried" before shooting himself in the head. On the other hand, if Shepard chastises the Illusive Man at his lust for control costing humanity the war, he angrily rebuts that notion and attempts to shoot Shepard but is shot first by the Commander instead. With his last breath, the Illusive Man looks through the Citadel arms and remarks how beautiful Earth is, wishing Shepard could see it the same way. The Catalyst, manifesting as the young boy Shepard saw killed during the fall of Earth, explains to Shepard that the Illusive Man was correct in believing that it was possible to take control of the Reapers; however, he would never have been able to do this himself, as the Reapers were already controlling him. The Illusive Man's final appearance is in the final decision at the Crucible, where he appears in a vision as the embodiment of the "Control" option.

This war-asset list collected the personnel, data and equipment that skilled operatives took with them when they abandoned Cerberus as the Illusive Man's methods grew more extreme. Equipment assets came from N7 missions: Cerberus Research Data (50), reports on Reaper unit composition used by Alliance military VIs, and an Advanced Fighter Squadron (75), fast fuel-efficient one-person craft captured on Noveria, repainted and pressed into Alliance service after being swept for bugs.

Personnel assets largely came from the Arrae: Ex-Cerberus Scientists mission. Ex-Cerberus Scientists (25) rescued from Gellix joined the Crucible project, as did their leader Dr. Brynn Cole (25), who had studied Collector technology and helped dozens of families flee Cerberus. Dr. Gavin Archer (25), a synthetic intelligence specialist from Terra Nova, contributed insights into parallel processing and the geth after David Archer was dealt with in Overlord and Grissom Academy was completed. Jacob Taylor (25) joined after an attack on a former-operative safehouse, working as a consultant on Cerberus tactics; he declined reinstatement into the Alliance marines.

Ex-Cerberus Engineers (10) were contacted by Kelly Chambers, who convinced former Cerberus engineers to come out of hiding and help build the Crucible. Miranda Lawson (25), the operative who led the Lazarus Cell that revived Shepard, brought extensive knowledge of the Illusive Man's operations to the Alliance. Cerberus Escapees (40-120, with a bug allowing 160), humans and aliens who broke out of a secret Cerberus holding facility, could be obtained only through the now-unavailable Mass Effect: Infiltrator mobile game.
evidence.for_key: the Illusive Man's control of Cerberus

evidence.text:
Priority: Cerberus Headquarters was a Mass Effect 3 mission, acquired immediately after Priority: Horizon and the events at Sanctuary, in which the Alliance assaulted the Illusive Man's base to recover the Prothean VI Vendetta, believed to hold the key to the Catalyst. The base was revealed to be Cronos Station, a space station orbiting Anadius in the Horse Head Nebula. Admiral Hackett warned Shepard over vidcomm that the attack would expose the Crucible to the Reapers and had to be treated as the first phase of the assault on the Reapers themselves; beginning the mission was the game's point of no return, after which side missions, DLC, and the Citadel became inaccessible. EDI was a mandatory squadmate.

Shepard's team fought through the station's hangar bay (stopping Cerberus from venting it into space), rotation and drive sections, and the remains of the Human-Reaper larva from Mass Effect 2. Depending on earlier choices, two named enemies could appear: Legion as a unique "Legion Assassin" if Shepard had turned it over to Cerberus, and an indoctrinated Jack as a unique Phantom if Grissom Academy had not been completed; both had to be killed. Video terminals along the route revealed details of the Lazarus Project, EDI's origin as the Rogue VI, Kai Leng, and Cerberus's Reaper implant research.

In the Illusive Man's inner sanctum, Shepard confronted him by hologram for the third time; Charm or Intimidate options carried consequences for the final confrontation on the Citadel. Vendetta then revealed that the Catalyst was the Citadel itself, but the Illusive Man, having overridden Vendetta's security, already knew this, had fled to the Citadel, and had alerted the Reapers, who seized the station and moved it to Earth. Kai Leng then attacked; after a running battle through the collapsing sanctum against Leng and three waves of Cerberus reinforcements, Shepard killed him, finishing him with an omni-blade after an optional Renegade interrupt. The team returned to the Normandy for a debrief with Anderson, and Priority: Earth became available, with Sol the only reachable system. Rewards included the M-37 Falcon, and the Reaper Heart or Brain War Asset depending on the Collector Base choice.
evidence.for_key: the Illusive Man's control of Cerberus

evidence.text:
This page is a chronological plot synopsis of the Mass Effect 3-era fiction.

In Mass Effect: Retribution, the Illusive Man had Kai Leng abduct former operative Paul Grayson and infected him with Reaper nanotech; Grayson, turned into a Reaper puppet, was hunted across the galaxy and finally killed at Grissom Academy by David Anderson, Kahlee Sanders and the student Nick. Mass Effect: Inquisition followed C-Sec's Bailey investigating Executor Pallin's supposed corruption at Udina's direction. Mass Effect: Deception continued the Kai Leng, Gillian Grayson and Biotic Underground threads. Mass Effect: Conviction had James Vega brought aboard the Normandy SR-2 to guard the imprisoned Shepard after the Bahak incident. Mass Effect: Invasion recounted Cerberus general Oleg Petrovsky and Colonel Raymond Ashe using an engineered Adjutant crisis to seize Omega from Aria T'Loak, who surrendered the station rather than see it destroyed. Mass Effect: Infiltrator followed rogue Cerberus operative Randall Ezno turning against the Director's Reaper-tech experiments after they mutilated his handler Inali Renata. Homeworlds #4 followed Liara T'Soni, now the Shadow Broker, chasing Prothean leads to Thessia and Kahje.

The Mass Effect 3 recap covered the Reaper invasion of Earth and Anderson staying behind; the Mars Archives and the discovery of the Prothean device (Crucible), with the android Eva Coré and EDI; the war summit and the genophage cure arc on Sur'Kesh and Tuchanka (Mordin Solus or Padok Wiks, Urdnot Wrex or Wreav, Dalatrass Linron, Primarch Adrien Victus, and Eve); the Cerberus coup on the Citadel and Udina's exposure and death; the quarian-geth war over Rannoch, ending in the destruction of a Reaper and peace or genocide; the fall of Thessia and Kai Leng's theft of the Prothean VI data; the pursuit of Cerberus through Sanctuary (Henry, Miranda and Oriana Lawson) to Cronos Station and Leng's death; and the battle for Earth. The synopsis closed with the Illusive Man's death, Anderson's death, and the Catalyst offering Shepard the Destroy, Control, Synthesis or refusal endings, followed by extensive epilogue variations and the Stargazer framing scene.
evidence.for_key: the Illusive Man's control of Cerberus

evidence.text: #### Mass Effect 2 |  | Audio: Cerberus (ME2\) | | --- | --- | Immediately following the First Contact War, an anonymous extranet manifesto warned that an alien attempt at human genocide was inevitable. The manifesto called for an army \-\- a Cerberus to guard against invasion through the Charon relay. Derided as "survivalist rhetoric written by an illusive man," the manifesto and its anonymous author soon fell off the media radar. But in 2165, terrorists stole antimatter from the SSV Geneva; the sole figure arrested named his sponsor "Cerberus." Throughout the 2160s and 2170s, alleged Cerberus agents assassinated politicians, sabotaged starships bearing eezo, and conducted nightmarish experiments on aliens and humans. Denounced as human\-supremacist, Cerberus calls itself human\-survivalist. Counterterror experts speculate Cerberus may have changed leadership with its recent shift to stockpiling ships, agents, and weapons. Whether "he," "she," or "they," the Illusive Man hides his finances behind shell companies. Few doubt he will kill anyone attempting to expose him. #### Mass Effect 3 |  | Audio: Cerberus (ME3\) | | --- | --- | In recent years, the pro\-human syndicate known as Cerberus has seen its influence grow galaxy\-wide. The largely untraceable organization now includes private intelligence agencies, biotics laboratories, research facilities, and the lucrative corporations that provide a front for it all. Cerberus's charismatic leader, known only as the Illusive Man, drives the organization's philosophy and interests. The level of secrecy he maintains puts professional intelligence agencies to shame. As Cerberus grows, so too does public distrust of the organization. Some commentators have remarked that Cerberus is not so much pro\-human as it is antialien. Others question the blind loyalty of its employees.

evidence.text:
This page catalogs single-use equipment items used during Mass Effect 3 multiplayer matches, each lasting one mission and grouped into ammo, armor and weapon bonuses. Ammo bonuses added a separate "ammo damage" component to shots, heavily modified by the target's current defense type. They included Armor-Piercing Rounds (damage and penetration versus armor, no bonus to shields or barriers), Cryo Rounds (slows, weakens armor, can freeze unshielded enemies to prime Cryo Explosions), Disruptor Rounds (4x damage to shields and barriers, primes Tech Bursts), Drill Rounds (long-range penetration through cover; from Retaliation), Explosive Rounds (delayed detonation; from Retaliation), Incendiary Rounds (damage-over-time, primes Fire Explosions, stops enemy health regeneration), Phasic Rounds (10x versus shields and barriers; from Retaliation), and Warp Rounds (armor weakening, bonus biotic damage against Biotic Explosion-primed targets, 2x versus barriers).

Armor bonuses covered the Adrenaline Module (movement speed), Cyclonic Modulator (shield strength up to +150%), Power Amplifier Module (power damage), Power Efficiency Module (recharge speed), Shield Power Cells (shorter shield recharge delay), and Stabilization Module (weapon stability). Weapon bonuses were the per-class Rail Amps (assault rifle, pistol, shotgun, SMG, sniper rifle; +10/20/30% damage), the Strength Enhancer (melee damage), and Targeting VI (headshot damage). Several items became available in Store packs only after downloading the Resurgence Pack, and drill, explosive and phasic rounds only after the Retaliation Pack. Each item had three or four escalating levels.

Amul Shastri was the Prime Minister of the Systems Alliance from at least 2185 until 2186. The date he took office and the length of his tenure were never recorded. By 2185 he had been involved in a public dispute with the CEO of a media company, who launched a campaign of mocking viral videos against Shastri until the Prime Minister backed down. Later that year Shastri met a salarian dalatrass during the salarian holiday of Betau and exchanged gifts with her; aware of his love of flying, she gave him a classic Tess Auburn 2166 aircar. He also attended the opening ceremonies of a public memorial and museum on Eden Prime after Earth's Council for the Preservation of Human History and Culture declared the colony a culturally significant site.

On August 24, 2186, Shastri addressed reporters at a news conference concerning a leaked report that appeared to support Commander Shepard's claims that the warship Sovereign, destroyed during the Battle of the Citadel, was not of geth construction but was one of many hostile machine intelligences. Shastri waved off questions, stated that the geth were not the only threat in the galaxy, and assured the public that the Alliance was prepared for anything.

Later in 2186, during the Reaper invasion, Shastri was killed along with the entire Alliance Parliament when Reaper forces destroyed Arcturus Station. With his death and the loss of the Parliament, Councilor Donnel Udina became the de facto political leader of the Alliance.

evidence.text: *See also: N7 Operations, Mass Effect 3 Multiplayer* During the Reaper war, Allied forces began recruiting anyone, soldier or mercenary, to serve on the front lines of the conflict. The most experienced operatives formed squads to secure objectives, evacuate civilians, and battle Cerberus or the Reapers deep in enemy territory. Initially led by N7 commandos, these squads were nicknamed the N7 Special Ops. In light of these teams' exemplary service and remarkable bravery, the Alliance allowed this unofficial name to spread across the ranks as a sign of respect for their efforts. N7 Special Ops teams can aid to varying degrees in the overall war effort.

Cerberus has operatives planted across Citadel space and the Terminus Systems who regularly report to the Illusive Man. Due to their widespread network, Cerberus effectively has access to almost every settled system, major trade stop, and colony in the galaxy. However, Cerberus has no knowledge of what goes on in uncharted systems and the Migrant Fleet, thus rendering the Illusive Man blind in those areas. Cerberus operatives usually work alone. If an operative is captured, depending on their usefulness, Cerberus might attempt a rescue or simply declare them to be expendable and abandon them to their captors.

“Strength for Cerberus is strength for every human. Cerberus is humanity.” **Cerberus** is a human\-supremacist paramilitary group led by the enigmatic Illusive Man. Couching itself as human\-survivalist, Cerberus' core belief is that humans deserve a greater role in the galactic community, and that the Systems Alliance is too hamstrung by law and public opinion to stand up effectively to the other Citadel races. Cerberus supports the principle that any methods of advancing humanity's ascension are entirely justified, including illegal or dangerous experimentation, terrorism, sabotage and assassination. Cerberus operatives accept that these methods are brutal but believe history will vindicate them. Nevertheless, both the Systems Alliance and the Citadel Council have declared Cerberus to be a terrorist organization and will prosecute identified Cerberus agents accordingly.

This page collects a promotional social-media broadcast BioWare ran to advertise the Mass Effect 3: Omega DLC. In the fiction, during 2186 Cerberus invaded and occupied the station Omega under General Oleg Petrovsky, having lured Aria T'Loak off-station, and a rebellion led by the Talon mercenary gang rose against them. A communication war followed across three comm channels: ANN (@AllianceNewsNet) reporting events and rumors, the Talons (@FightForOmega) broadcasting on low-tech microwave emissions in "Talon Cryptolect," and Cerberus (@Omega_Cerberus), Petrovsky's official citizen feed of directives and propaganda. The Talons hacked ANN to recruit "Codebreakers" to decrypt Cerberus's coded messages, which used a simple substitution cipher. The messages track skirmishes through the Fumi and Zeta Districts, with Nyreen Kandros drawing Cerberus forces away so extraction teams could evacuate civilians.

Representative lines:

Nyreen Kandros / the Talons, opening broadcast: "Cerberus may have taken over Omega, but that doesn't mean they've won. This is our territory. Our home. ... The Talons have not abandoned you. We shall not rest until Cerberus is out of Omega and your homes are returned to you."

Cerberus, propaganda feed: "As we secure Omega against Reaper incursions, please cooperate with all Cerberus directives. Your safety is our top priority."

Cerberus, recruiting: "Cerberus is recruiting! No experience? No problem! Our orientation provides combat training and gene therapy packages. Change your life now!"

General Petrovsky, quoted on the Cerberus feed: "The civilized being prizes freedom above all. Yet civilization itself is only possible through unyielding discipline."

Nyreen Kandros, spotted in Fumi District: "Base leaders, codebreakers are reporting I've been spotted by Cerberus forces. Looks like I'm the decoy."

Cerberus, decoded cipher message: "Locking down Fumi District due to persistent Talon activity. Full purge authorized--get every Talon. Petrovsky's orders."

Nyreen Kandros, closing: "Cerberus may have the upper hand, but they can't keep us down. We're all in this together, Omega civilians and friends alike."

Cerberus Snipers were operatives employed by Cerberus to defend its installations and research facilities in the first Mass Effect. They guarded the exterior and interior of key sites on Binthu and Nepheron, where Cerberus conducted research on captured organisms including Rachni Workers, Rachni Soldiers and Thorian Creepers. Armed with sniper rifles, they preferred to keep their distance and frequently used the Assassination ability, though its red sighting laser telegraphed the shot and made it easy to dodge. Because they held back at range, dislodging them usually required biotic or tech attacks. The page notes equivalent enemies elsewhere in the series: the Sniper in Mass Effect: Infiltrator and the Nemesis in Mass Effect 3.

Designed with three things in mind: shields, thick armor, and auxiliary ammo packs, the Cerberus Assault Armor is given to shock troopers who are expected to turn the tide of battle against forces that would decimate normal soldiers. Additionally, the M\-22 Eviscerator Shotgun comes standard issue. Lethal at close range, the Eviscerator Shotgun is a favorite among Cerberus operatives who like to get up close and personal with their foes.

The Project Phoenix Adept was a playable multiplayer class in Mass Effect 3, one of the Project Phoenix operatives. Project Phoenix was a result of the Illusive Man's early experiments in enhanced human physiology, producing highly skilled combat and biotic specialists. When the Illusive Man turned to indoctrination to guarantee the loyalty of his troops, many Phoenix operatives defected and joined the Alliance to fight the Reapers. Their mastery of Cerberus lash and stasis technology, combined with powerful biotics, made them valued battlefield assets.

The Adept had 500 barrier and 500 health and used the powers Singularity, Lash, Smash and Fitness under Phoenix Training. Its regular melee was a shock baton strike hitting up to two enemies; its heavy melee swung biotically charged Cerberus lashes; and its grab dragged an enemy over cover for a charged biotic punch. Singularity primed biotic explosions on all enemies and could be chained into double explosions with Lash or Smash. Lash functioned like a damaging, long-range Pull that could be evolved to penetrate shields and barriers. Smash was a short-range, cover-piercing attack devastating against infantry and armored bosses but leaving the user briefly vulnerable. The class's main weakness was dealing with heavy enemies such as Banshees, Brutes, Atlases, Geth Pyros and Geth Primes, since Smash's short range forced dangerous proximity.
